title: South Korea's transport ministry plans AI cameras that alert train drivers to vehicles or pedestrians trapped at crossings, with pilots at Nonsan and Boseong before 543 crossings nationwide
summary: South Korea's transport ministry plans AI cameras from an unnamed supplier to detect vehicles or pedestrians trapped at crossings and alert drivers, with pilots at Nonsan and Boseong.
account: Kyunghyang Shinmun's 최미랑 reported on 11 February 2026 that the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport had drawn up a comprehensive railway-crossing accident-prevention plan. It was to take effect from March 2026. It includes an AI-based intelligent closed-circuit television (CCTV) system, to be installed in railway protection zones nationwide. The system immediately detects a vehicle or pedestrian trapped inside a crossing. It then transmits the information to the driver of an approaching train. Pilot installations were planned within the first quarter at Nonsan in Chungnam and at Boseong, where accidents occurred in 2025. Installation at the 543 national crossings would follow in sequence, depending on the results. The plan also adds fines of up to 70,000 won, after a six-month grace period. They apply to vehicles that fail to stop or that enter while barriers operate. The ministry cited 36 crossing accidents over five years with 14 deaths and 7 injuries, 27 of them due to driver carelessness. No source names a developer. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor labels the announcement an AI hazard. Newspim reported on 10 July 2026 that the ministry still planned to install the AI cameras at the Nonsan and Boseong crossings, after the first-quarter target had passed. On 23 September 2026 the ministry and Korail said that crossing cameras were in pilot operation and that they would consider a phased expansion. No source reports results.
purpose: The AI CCTV is intended to detect vehicles or pedestrians trapped in crossings and warn approaching train drivers in time to stop.

display.answer: Kyunghyang Shinmun reported the ministry's announcement of the plan. Newspim and The Power News repeat later announcements of the ministry, the second made with Korail. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor lists the February announcement as an AI hazard.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: South Korea's transport ministry plans AI cameras from an unnamed supplier to detect vehicles or pedestrians trapped at crossings and alert drivers, with pilots at Nonsan and Boseong.
fields.account: Kyunghyang Shinmun's 최미랑 reported on 11 February 2026 that the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport had drawn up a comprehensive railway-crossing accident-prevention plan. It was to take effect from March 2026. It includes an AI-based intelligent closed-circuit television (CCTV) system, to be installed in railway protection zones nationwide. The system immediately detects a vehicle or pedestrian trapped inside a crossing. It then transmits the information to the driver of an approaching train. Pilot installations were planned within the first quarter at Nonsan in Chungnam and at Boseong, where accidents occurred in 2025. Installation at the 543 national crossings would follow in sequence, depending on the results. The plan also adds fines of up to 70,000 won, after a six-month grace period. They apply to vehicles that fail to stop or that enter while barriers operate. The ministry cited 36 crossing accidents over five years with 14 deaths and 7 injuries, 27 of them due to driver carelessness. No source names a developer. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor labels the announcement an AI hazard. Newspim reported on 10 July 2026 that the ministry still planned to install the AI cameras at the Nonsan and Boseong crossings, after the first-quarter target had passed. On 23 September 2026 the ministry and Korail said that crossing cameras were in pilot operation and that they would consider a phased expansion. No source reports results.
